en: finish with a thread of oil

does: Pours a thin thread of oil or dressing over a finished dish just before it is served, so that every part gets a little and the oil keeps its fresh taste.

intro.what: Drizzling lays a thin thread of oil over a plated dish.
intro.why: Raw oil added last keeps its fresh scent and coats everything lightly without making it soggy.

how: Hold the bottle or a spoon above the dish and pour in a thin, moving thread, back and forth.
Do it at the last moment, at the table if you can.

cues.text: A fine, glossy thread over every part, with no pool at the bottom.
The fresh, green smell of the oil.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in a puddle, so some parts swim and others stay dry.
Dressing too early, so the salad turns watery.

quiz.question: Why is the oil added at the last moment?
choices: So it keeps its fresh scent and the food stays crisp.
quiz.because: Fresh oil added last tastes brightest.

quiz.question: How do you pour?
choices: In one puddle in the middle.
In a thin thread moved over the whole dish.
Over the plate before the food.
quiz.because: A moving thread spreads it evenly.

quiz.question: What should you see?
choices: A pool of oil on the plate.
A fine glossy thread over every part.

quiz.question: The plate ended up swimming in oil. What would you change?
choices: Pour a thinner thread and less of it.
